name: Mastitis
standard_protocol: Strip the quarter out. Intramammary antibiotic per sensitivity, plus systemic cover if febrile. NSAID for pain. Mark the cow and milk her last.
typical_symptoms: Swollen, hot, painful quarter. Clots or flakes in milk. Drop in yield. Fever in acute cases.

name: Foot and Mouth Disease
standard_protocol: NOTIFIABLE — report to the veterinary authority immediately. No treatment; supportive care and strict isolation. Movement standstill.
typical_symptoms: Drooling, blisters on tongue and gums, lameness, vesicles in the interdigital space, sharp drop in milk yield.

name: Lumpy Skin Disease
standard_protocol: NOTIFIABLE. Supportive care, antibiotic cover against secondary infection, fly control. Vaccinate the rest of the herd.
typical_symptoms: Firm raised skin nodules over the body, enlarged lymph nodes, fever, nasal discharge, reduced yield.

name: East Coast Fever
standard_protocol: Buparvaquone early — outcome depends almost entirely on how soon it is given. Supportive fluids. Tick control across the herd.
typical_symptoms: Grossly swollen parotid lymph node, high fever, laboured breathing, frothy nasal discharge, rapid loss of condition.

name: Brucellosis
standard_protocol: NOTIFIABLE and ZOONOTIC — handle aborted material with gloves. No treatment; test and cull reactors. Vaccinate replacements.
typical_symptoms: Abortion in the last trimester, retained placenta, weak calves, reduced fertility. Often silent in the herd.

name: Milk Fever
standard_protocol: Intravenous calcium borogluconate slowly, watching the heart. Follow with oral calcium. Review dry-cow mineral balance.
typical_symptoms: Unsteady gait then recumbency within 48 hours of calving, cold extremities, S-shaped neck kink, no rumen movement.

name: Ketosis
standard_protocol: Oral propylene glycol, dextrose IV in severe cases. Correct the negative energy balance in the transition ration.
typical_symptoms: Reduced appetite in early lactation, sweet acetone smell on the breath, falling yield, weight loss.

name: Bloat
standard_protocol: Pass a stomach tube. Anti-foaming agent for frothy bloat. Trocarisation only as a last resort. Review lush legume access.
typical_symptoms: Distended left flank, distress, laboured breathing, drooling. Can kill within an hour.

name: Lameness - Foot Rot
standard_protocol: Trim and clean the foot, topical antibiotic, systemic antibiotic if swelling extends. Footbath the herd; fix underfoot conditions.
typical_symptoms: Sudden lameness in one limb, swelling above the hoof, foul-smelling interdigital lesion.

name: Calf Scours
standard_protocol: Oral rehydration first and repeatedly — dehydration kills, not the pathogen. Keep milk feeding. Antibiotic only where blood or fever is present. Check colostrum management.
typical_symptoms: Watery diarrhoea in calves under a month, sunken eyes, skin tenting, weakness, refusal to suck.

name: Retained Placenta
standard_protocol: Do not pull. Systemic antibiotic and NSAID if febrile. Recheck at 48 hours; treat resulting metritis. Review calcium and vitamin E status.
typical_symptoms: Membranes still hanging more than 12 hours after calving, foul discharge, possible fever.

name: Trypanosomiasis
standard_protocol: Diminazene aceturate. Tsetse control around the grazing. Watch for relapse and for drug resistance in endemic areas.
typical_symptoms: Intermittent fever, progressive anaemia with pale membranes, weight loss despite feed, enlarged lymph nodes.
